P0300.title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
P0300.description: The engine module detects misfire from crankshaft speed: a cylinder that does not fire gives no acceleration impulse. At a catalyst-damaging rate (CARB: at least 5 % per 200 revolutions) the warning light flashes; at an emissions-relevant rate (at least 1 % per 1,000 revolutions – GM about 2–5 %, Ford 0.9–1.5 %) it comes on after two trips. Ford and GM may shut off a misfiring cylinder's injector to protect the catalyst. P0300 sets when the misfire cannot be assigned to one cylinder: several cylinders each account for more than 10 %, the cylinder changes randomly, or – at Ford – the cylinder cannot be identified at high speed. It often appears together with cylinder codes. Causes are usually systemic: false air, worn plugs on several cylinders, fuel pressure or fuel quality, valve timing – and false detection from a damaged tone wheel, rough roads or vibration. Bulletins name coils, cracked plug insulators and wrong plug gaps.

causes.label: False air (vacuum leak, crankcase ventilation, intake gasket)
Worn or wrong spark plugs on several cylinders, faulty ignition coils
Fuel pressure too low or high, contaminated fuel
Valve timing (stretched chain), valves, compression on several cylinders
False detection: tone wheel or pulley, rough road, vibration, software

symptoms: Check engine light on, flashing at a catalyst-damaging rate
Smell of unburnt fuel, higher consumption

P030A.title: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit/Open
P030A.description: Ignition A is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff). P030A means the control line is open – the module sees a voltage with its driver off that indicates high resistance. No manufacturer using these codes was found; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff (open above 30 kΩ, first trip), so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.

causes.label: Control line or connector pin open (corrosion, pushed-back pin)
Ignition module or coil with integrated driver of this group faulty
Supply or ground of the ignition module faulty
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power, possibly cylinders shut off

P0313.title: Misfire Detected with Low Fuel
P0313.description: When the tank is nearly empty the fuel pump can draw air in corners or on gradients, which causes misfires. CARB allows misfire detection to be switched off at 15 % fuel or less; some manufacturers instead report misfires detected in this state under P0313 rather than P030x. Ford's normal misfire monitor runs from 15 % fuel, Saab's ME9 from 12 %; Saab's T8 sets P0313 below 5 litres with the same tests as P0300 (3 % per 1,000 revolutions, flashing light at a catalyst-damaging rate). GM petrol engines simply suspend the monitor without their own code. After refuelling the symptoms usually disappear – if not, look for a real misfire cause.

causes.label: Tank nearly empty – the fuel pump draws air (corners, gradients, braking)
Actual misfire cause (ignition, injector, false air) that happened at low fuel
Weak fuel pump, clogged strainer or filter, faulty swirl pot
Fuel level sender reading too low

symptoms: Check engine light on (flashing at a catalyst-damaging rate)
Jerking or power loss with an almost empty tank, especially in corners or uphill

P0314.title: Single Cylinder Misfire (Cylinder Not Specified)
P0314.description: P0314 means the misfire is attributable to a single cylinder, but the module does not say which one. CARB generally requires cylinder-specific codes and allows a general code only with approval where the cylinder cannot be identified reliably; for diesels identification is required only where possible without extra hardware. GM and Ford do not use P0314. It is documented on Saab's 2.2 TiD diesel with a Bosch distributor pump, as a mechanical misfire fault in two speed and quantity windows with the warning light and limp mode limiting injection quantity; the cylinder can still be read out with a scan tool. Typical causes are a faulty injector, leaking high-pressure lines, air or water in the fuel, or low compression.

causes.label: Injector of one cylinder clogged or leaking (diesel), or coil/plug (petrol)
Leaking high-pressure line, fuel bridge or injector washer
Air, water or petrol in the diesel, clogged filter, low supply pressure
Compression loss (valve, piston)

symptoms: Loss of power, limp mode with quantity limit (Saab diesel)

P0315.title: Crankshaft Position System Variation Not Learned
P0315.description: Manufacturing tolerances of the crankshaft tone wheel distort the speed fluctuations misfire detection relies on, so the engine module learns a correction for each tooth or segment. P0315 means these values have not been learned or are invalid. GM checks that the learned tooth angles add up to 360° (deviation above 0.001° sets the code in the first trip) and learns them with a scan tool: brakes held, full throttle in park until fuel cut-off. Ford learns the profile during up to three overrun phases from 60 to 40 mph and sets P0315 when that fails. Until relearned, misfire detection is suspended – at GM above 1,000 rpm – and misfire readiness stays incomplete. The relearn is needed after replacing the engine, engine module, crankshaft, damper or crankshaft sensor.

causes.label: Relearn not performed after replacing sensor, crankshaft, damper, engine or engine module
Learned values lost through voltage loss (battery disconnected)
Tone wheel damaged or shifted, crankshaft runout, dirt on the sensor
Interference in the crankshaft sensor circuit
Engine module memory faulty

symptoms: Check engine light on (GM; Ford depending on application)
Misfire readiness not set – emissions test fails

P0316.title: Engine Misfire Detected on Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)

Typical causes are water in the plug wells (Mazda Tribute bulletin: blocked drain in the valve cover channel), coils that arc when cold and damp, injectors that drip after switch-off and over-rich starting – Ford traced cases on the 2.7 EcoBoost to engine software or leaking direct injectors.

causes.label: Moisture or water in the plug wells, coils arcing when cold or damp

Worn or sooted spark plugs that only fire cleanly when warm

symptoms: Rough running right after a cold start, then normal
Delayed start, fuel smell at start

P0317.title: Rough Road Hardware Not Present
P0317.description: Misfire detection works from crankshaft speed fluctuations, which rough roads also cause. CARB therefore allows misfire detection to pause on rough roads; many engines take a rough-road signal from the wheel speeds of the ABS module, a Ford patent describes such a detector. P0317 means the engine module is calibrated for an external rough-road signal but does not find the hardware: the supplying module does not respond on the data bus, or the configuration does not match the equipment – for example after replacing the engine or ABS module. Without the signal misfire detection cannot separate road bumps from misfires. No manufacturer document using P0317 was found; the description follows CARB and GM's rough-road sources in its misfire monitor.

causes.label: Module configuration does not match the equipment (after engine or ABS module replacement)
ABS/ESP module not responding (supply, CAN line)
Separate rough-road sensor missing or unplugged, where fitted
Engine module faulty

symptoms: Possibly false misfire codes on rough roads

causes.label: Wheel speed sensor or wiring faulty – the brake module passes on the fault

Brake control module faulty
Separate rough-road sensor faulty, where fitted

P0335.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit

P0338.description: By its J2012 name P0338 means the crankshaft position signal stays at a high level – signal wire shorted to supply, or an open signal output that the module's pull-up holds high on a Hall sensor. GM 2014–2019 and Ford do not use the code. GM's Global A engines in the Saab 9-5 (2010/11) and 9-4X define it as a high duty cycle, i.e. too many pulses or teeth between the reference gaps: on the 2.8 turbo V6 (LAU) a deviation of more than 8 teeth, checked once per revolution and set in the first trip; on the 1.6 (LLU) more than 200 reference pulses in 10 revolutions, and on the 2.0 turbo (LDK) a large tooth deviation over 4 revolutions, both after two trips. Behind this are usually interference pulses or a gap that is not recognised. Result: misfire, stalling, limp mode.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to supply or open (pull-up holds the level high)
Interference pulses from poor ground or shielding
Crankshaft position sensor faulty
Tone wheel damaged or dirty (gap not recognised)

P0339.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0339.description: P0339 means the crankshaft position signal drops out or is disturbed for moments and then recovers. Ford's 2020–2023 petrol engines use it, depending on the engine, instead of P0320 for tooth errors: wrong tooth count after the gap, tooth time outside 30 to 9,000 rpm, gap at an unexpected position, from 500 rpm, detected within 5 s. In Ford's PCM code list (Roush workshop manual) P0339 is listed without check engine light. Saab's 9-3 diesel (T8) counts dropouts: more than 8 within 10 ms over 3 s, or more than 3 in a whole drive cycle. Honda recalled 2023 Accord Hybrids because a mis-machined sensor mounting caused no-start, rough idle, hunting idle and P0017 with P0339. Typical causes are a loose contact, a sensor failing when hot and a wrong air gap.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector or an in-line connector
Sensor dropping out when hot
Sensor mounting or air gap mechanically wrong (machining error, bracket)
Electrical interference
Tone wheel slightly damaged

symptoms: Check engine light on (not on all Ford engines)

P033A.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit
P033A.description: The knock sensor is a piezoelectric structure-borne sound sensor bolted to the engine block; the module evaluates its signal per cylinder and retards ignition when it detects knock. Sensor D is a fourth sensor on engines with four knock sensors (McLaren 12C V8, Ford's 2020–23 systems). With a fault the module retards ignition across the board as protection – noticeable loss of power and higher consumption. P033A means the sensor circuit is open or the signal stays below the noise threshold. GM feeds a 20 kHz test signal into the circuit and detects an open circuit when it does not cancel out, setting the code in the first trip; Ford sees any open or short as a knock signal that is too small compared with the speed- and load-dependent noise level (at least 1,500 rpm, 35 % load, warm engine).

causes.label: Wiring or connector chafed, broken or corroded (sensor often under the intake manifold)
Knock sensor faulty (cracked piezo, moisture, heat damage)
Sensor loose or wrongly torqued
Engine software or diagnostic calibration
Engine module input stage

symptoms: Loss of power, sluggish response from ignition retard

P033B.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit Range/Performance
P033B.description: The knock sensor is a piezoelectric structure-borne sound sensor bolted to the engine block; the module evaluates its signal per cylinder and retards ignition when it detects knock. Sensor D is a fourth sensor on engines with four knock sensors (McLaren 12C V8, Ford's 2020–23 systems). With a fault the module retards ignition across the board as protection – noticeable loss of power and higher consumption. P033B means the circuit is electrically sound but the signal is implausible. GM sets it when the filtered background noise stays below a threshold – typically a loose sensor or one not bolted down properly – in the first trip; Saab's GM-based engines also when excessive knock persists on several cylinders or a whole bank for 8–10 s. Ford does not use this code. Only McLaren lists this code for its four-sensor V8; thresholds follow the sensor A/B checks.

causes.label: Sensor loose, wrongly torqued or mounted with sealant or on a dirty surface
Engine software or calibration (bulletins for some models)
Genuine knock on a whole bank or mechanical noise
Sensor aged or damaged (low sensitivity)

symptoms: Loss of power, sluggish response from ignition retard

P033C.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit Low
P033C.description: The knock sensor is a piezoelectric structure-borne sound sensor bolted to the engine block; the module evaluates its signal per cylinder and retards ignition when it detects knock. Sensor D is a fourth sensor on engines with four knock sensors (McLaren 12C V8, Ford's 2020–23 systems). With a fault the module retards ignition across the board as protection – noticeable loss of power and higher consumption. P033C means the diagnostic DC voltage at the sensor input is too low – the signal or return wire is shorted to ground. GM biases each input through a resistor network and sets the code below 8 % of 5 V in 50 of 63 samples, in the first trip; Ford checks actively once every 250 engine cycles on modules with this circuit.

causes.label: Signal or return wire chafed to ground
Moisture or corrosion in connector or sensor
Sensor faulty internally (series issue on some models)
Engine module internal

symptoms: Loss of power, sluggish response from ignition retard

P033D.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit High
P033D.description: The knock sensor is a piezoelectric structure-borne sound sensor bolted to the engine block; the module evaluates its signal per cylinder and retards ignition when it detects knock. Sensor D is a fourth sensor on engines with four knock sensors (McLaren 12C V8, Ford's 2020–23 systems). With a fault the module retards ignition across the board as protection – noticeable loss of power and higher consumption. P033D means the diagnostic DC voltage at the sensor input is too high – typically a short to voltage. GM sets it above 39 % of 5 V in 50 of 63 samples, in the first trip; Ford checks actively once every 250 engine cycles on modules with this circuit.

causes.label: Signal or return wire shorted to voltage
Corrosion or moisture in the connector
Sensor faulty internally
Engine module internal

symptoms: Loss of power, sluggish response from ignition retard

P033E.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit Intermittent
P033E.description: The knock sensor is a piezoelectric structure-borne sound sensor bolted to the engine block; the module evaluates its signal per cylinder and retards ignition when it detects knock. Sensor D is a fourth sensor on engines with four knock sensors (McLaren 12C V8, Ford's 2020–23 systems). With a fault the module retards ignition across the board as protection – noticeable loss of power and higher consumption. P033E reports brief dropouts of the sensor signal – loose contacts, a wire breaking with engine movement and heat, or a loose sensor. No manufacturer document with a threshold for this code was found; GM and Ford cover such faults with their circuit codes, so the description follows CARB's input monitoring requirement.

causes.label: Loose contact, spread pins or corrosion in the connector
Wire chafing only with engine movement or heat
Sensor loose or wrongly torqued
Sensor or engine module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power, sluggish response from ignition retard

P033F.title: Crankshaft/Camshaft Loss Of Synchronization
P033F.description: To know which stroke each cylinder is in, the engine module matches the crank angle with the camshaft phase. P033F means this synchronisation is lost while running or cannot be established. It is documented by code only at Ford (2020–2023): P033F, as an alternative to Ford's older own code, stands for a disturbed crank signal without crank/cam synchronisation, and then misfire detection is also impossible. Ford's 2012 description shows the reaction: on a crank sensor fault the module cuts fuel and spark and resynchronises – one revolution to find the gap, one more to confirm cylinder 1 via the camshaft sensor. FCA evaluates the same function in its own cam/crank synchronisation monitor under other codes. Besides the sensors, a jumped timing chain or belt can be behind it.

causes.label: Noisy or disturbed crankshaft signal (sensor, air gap, interference)
Disturbed camshaft signal
Timing chain or belt jumped or heavily stretched
Wiring or connector
Tone wheel damaged or loose

P0340.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Bank 1 or Single Sensor
P0340.description: The camshaft position sensor, almost always a Hall sensor, tells the engine module which stroke cylinder 1 is in – one crank revolution alone is ambiguous – and measures the actual cam phase with variable timing. Sensor A is the intake camshaft, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. P0340 means no or too few cam pulses arrive while the crankshaft turns in sync. GM sets it after 5.5 s (or 4 s) of cranking without a cam pulse or fewer than 4 pulses in 3 s running, petrol engines after two trips. Ford checks the ratio of cam to crank events from 200 rpm. The engine usually keeps running but starts longer and loses power as cam timing is held. Bulletins: corroded connectors on GM V8s (PIP5335C), moisture in the oil on short trips in Ford hybrids (SSM 48598).

causes.label: Camshaft position sensor faulty (heat, moisture)
Connector or wiring corroded or open, 5 V reference disturbed
Tone wheel on the camshaft or phaser damaged, loose or at the wrong distance
Timing drive jumped or wrongly assembled
Moisture in the engine oil from short trips (Ford hybrids)

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0341.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 or Single Sensor
P0341.description: P0341 means the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) delivers pulses, but their number or pattern does not fit the crankshaft. GM counts the pulses while the crank is in sync: 4 to 6 in the first 12 reference events and 398 to 402 per 100 engine cycles on the 4X wheel of the cam phaser; outside that in 8 of 10 checks the code is set after two trips. Ford's 2023 diesel compares the detected segment profile of the cam wheel with the expected one (1.2 s); the Saab 9-4X V6 checks pulses per crank revolution and correlation with crank position. Ford petrol engines use P0344 instead. Result: cam phase uncertain, cam timing switched off, possibly hard starting. GM names corroded connectors at the timing cover as a sporadic cause (PIP5335C).

causes.label: Sensor with interference pulses or weak signal, air gap
Tone wheel on the phaser damaged or wrongly fitted
Connector or wiring fault (corrosion, interference)
Crankshaft signal disturbed (wrong reference)

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0342.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Low Bank 1 or Single Sensor
P0342.description: P0342 means the signal of the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) stays at ground level without edges – signal wire shorted to ground, sensor supply missing or the Hall sensor faulty. Ford's 2023 diesel sets it when the signal stays at 0 V over 10 or more crank revolutions (3 s), while cranking or running. On the Saab 9-4X V6 (GM LAU) the signal must stay low without pulses for more than 1 s, or 10 s cumulatively, and the code follows after two trips; with the sensor disconnected the signal wire should show 4.8–5.2 V. Saab's Motronic 2.8.1 (900 V6) treats low and high together: no connection or short to ground or battery, about 4.5 V at idle, air gap at most 1.5 mm. GM petrol engines 2014–2019 and Ford petrol engines report this under P0340.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
5 V or 12 V supply of the sensor missing
Camshaft position sensor faulty
Connector corroded or wiring chafed

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0343.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit High Bank 1 or Single Sensor
P0343.description: P0343 means the signal of the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) stays at supply level without edges. Causes are a signal wire shorted to positive, an open signal wire that the module's pull-up holds at 5 V, a broken sensor ground or a faulty sensor. Ford's 2023 diesel sets it when the signal stays at system voltage over 10 or more crank revolutions (3 s). On the Saab 9-4X V6 (GM LAU) the signal must stay high without pulses for more than 1 s, or 10 s cumulatively, and the code follows after two trips. Saab's Motronic 2.8.1 (900 V6) treats low and high together and allows an air gap of at most 1.5 mm. The consequences are as for P0340: longer cranking, cam timing switched off, loss of power.

causes.label: Signal wire open or shorted to positive
Sensor ground open
Camshaft position sensor faulty
Connector corroded

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0344.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent Bank 1 or Single Sensor
P0344.description: P0344 means the signal of the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) is disturbed for moments: edges are missing or appear at an unexpected angle. Ford checks this on the five-tooth wheel used with variable cam timing; if edges appear where none are expected, Ford sets P0344 and switches cam timing off (loss of power and torque), from 200 rpm, detected within 5 s. In Ford hybrids (C-Max, Fusion, MKZ 2013–2020) moisture in the engine oil from short trips caused P0340 and P0344 – remedy: new sensor and oil change (SSM 48598). FCA asks for the cam/crank synchronisation event data to be saved before replacing a cam sensor. The 2010 Saab 9-5 2.0 diesel uses P0344 differently for too few cam pulses.

causes.label: Moisture or oil inside the sensor, dropping out when hot
Loose contact or corrosion at the connector
Tone wheel on the phaser damaged or loose
Interference or chafed wiring
Crankshaft signal disturbed (wrong reference)

symptoms: Sporadic loss of power (cam timing off)

P0345.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Bank 2
P0345.description: P0345 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0340: the intake camshaft sensor on the side without cylinder 1 – only on V and boxer engines with one cam sensor per bank – delivers no or too few pulses while the crankshaft turns in sync. GM uses the same criteria as for P0340, e.g. on the 3.0 twin-turbo V6 (LGW): 5.5 s or 4 s of cranking without a cam pulse, or fewer than 4 pulses in 3 s running, set after two trips. Ford checks the ratio of cam to crank events from 200 rpm, detected within 5 s. FCA lists P0345 among the cam sensor codes for which the synchronisation event data should be saved before replacing the sensor. Result: cam timing on bank 2 is switched off and power drops; the cam phase usually remains available from the bank 1 sensor.

causes.label: Camshaft position sensor bank 2 faulty
Connector or wiring of bank 2 corroded or open
Tone wheel or phaser of bank 2 damaged
Timing drive of bank 2 jumped

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0346.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2
P0346.description: P0346 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0341: the intake camshaft sensor on the side without cylinder 1 delivers pulses, but their number or pattern does not fit the crankshaft. GM applies the same counting criteria as for P0341, e.g. on the 3.0 twin-turbo V6 (LGW): 4 to 6 pulses in the first 12 reference events and 398 to 402 per 100 engine cycles on the 4X wheel, set after two trips. On the Saab 9-4X V6 (GM LAU) the code means too many or too few pulses per crank revolution, or no correlation with crank position, for more than 1 s or 10 s cumulatively, also after two trips. Ford petrol engines do not use the code and report such faults under P0349. Result: cam timing on bank 2 switched off, loss of power, rough running.

causes.label: Bank 2 sensor with disturbed signal, air gap
Tone wheel on the bank 2 phaser damaged or wrongly fitted
Connector, wiring or interference
Crankshaft reference signal disturbed

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0347.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Low Bank 2
P0347.description: P0347 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0342: the signal of the intake camshaft sensor on the side without cylinder 1 stays at ground level without edges – signal wire shorted to ground, sensor supply missing or the sensor faulty. A code-specific manufacturer description exists only from GM: on the Saab 9-4X V6 (GM LAU) the signal must stay low without pulses for more than 1 s, or 10 s cumulatively, and the code follows after two trips. GM's other engines of 2014–2019 and Ford report such faults under P0345. Saab's 3.0 TiD diesel (2002) uses P0347 differently for a missing cam signal over 24 crank revolutions from 600 rpm. Result: cam timing on bank 2 switched off, loss of power, possibly longer cranking.

causes.label: Bank 2 signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor supply missing
Camshaft position sensor bank 2 faulty
Connector or wiring damaged

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0348.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit High Bank 2
P0348.description: P0348 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0343: the signal of the intake camshaft sensor on the side without cylinder 1 stays at supply level without edges. Causes are a signal wire shorted to positive, an open signal wire held high by the module's pull-up, a broken sensor ground or a faulty sensor. A code-specific manufacturer description exists only from GM: on the Saab 9-4X V6 (GM LAU) the signal must stay high without pulses for more than 1 s, or 10 s cumulatively, and the code follows after two trips. Ford's 2023 diesel shows the same check on bank 1 (P0343: system voltage over 10 or more crank revolutions). Other GM engines and Ford petrol engines report such faults under P0345. Result: cam timing on bank 2 switched off, loss of power.

causes.label: Bank 2 signal wire open or shorted to positive
Sensor ground open
Camshaft position sensor bank 2 faulty
Connector corroded

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0349.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent Bank 2
P0349.description: P0349 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0344: the signal of the intake camshaft sensor on the side without cylinder 1 is disturbed for moments – edges are missing or appear at an unexpected angle. Ford checks this on the five-tooth wheel used with variable cam timing; if edges appear where none are expected, Ford sets P0349 and switches cam timing on bank 2 off, from 200 rpm, detected within 5 s. FCA also uses the code and asks for the cam/crank synchronisation event data to be saved before the sensor is replaced, because a disturbed crank reference can look like a cam fault. GM does not use P0349. Typical causes are a loose contact at the bank 2 connector, a sensor dropping out when hot or soaked with oil moisture, and a damaged tone wheel.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the bank 2 connector
Sensor dropping out when hot or due to oil moisture
Tone wheel of bank 2 damaged
Interference or chafed wiring

symptoms: Sporadic loss of power (cam timing off)

P034A.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor - Crankshaft Start Position Incorrect
P034A.description: Engines with start-stop or hybrid autostart store the crankshaft rest position when the engine stops, so that they can inject and fire correctly at once on restart. This needs a direction-sensing crank sensor, because a cylinder under compression can push the crankshaft backwards after shut-off. On restart the module compares the stored position with the one actually measured after the reference gap. GM sets P034A when they differ by more than 2 teeth in 2 of 3 autostarts or by at least 1 tooth in 4 of 5, after two trips; the diesel already at more than 1 tooth in 1 of 3. The check is suspended while a crank sensor fault is present. Result: start-stop is restricted, restarts take longer with conventional synchronisation, and the autostart may be rough.

causes.label: Direction-sensing crankshaft position sensor faulty or aged
Interference pulses in the sensor circuit during shut-off
Air gap or tone wheel – teeth not detected at low speed
Engine module software

P034B.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor - Crankshaft Direction Incorrect
P034B.description: Direction-sensing (bidirectional) crank sensors count the rest position for start-stop even when the crankshaft rocks back after shut-off. In normal running the sensor must never report reverse rotation – if it does, the signal is disturbed. GM sets P034B after at least 3 direction reversals within 10 s at 400 to 2,000 rpm and an airflow of at least 1.5 g/s, after two trips; the diesel uses the same thresholds. GM bulletin 17-NA-317 describes the 3.6 V6 (LFY) in the 2018 Buick Enclave and Chevrolet Traverse: interference in the sensor circuit caused P034B with P0506, low idle or stalling after an autostart, transmission slip above 65 km/h and cruise control dropping out; the remedy was a revised sensor wiring. Result: start-stop disabled, possibly reduced power.

causes.label: Interference in the sensor circuit (wiring routed next to switching lines)
Direction-sensing crankshaft position sensor faulty
Ground or connector fault
Tone wheel or air gap

symptoms: Low idle or stalling after an autostart
Follow-on effects such as transmission slip or cruise control dropping out (GM LFY)

P034C.title: Ion Sense System Performance
P034C.description: With ion current sensing the spark plug serves as a sensor after the spark: a measuring voltage across the gap drives a current through the ions in the flame, from which the module detects combustion, misfire and knock – a Delphi patent describes coils with built-in ion sensing, and Saab's Trionic engines detected misfire this way. P034C means this measuring system works implausibly, so misfire and knock detection are no longer reliable. It is documented on the Alfa Romeo Giulia and Stelvio 2.9 V6 biturbo, where three bulletins fix it mainly with engine software; limp mode is possible. Sooted plugs or a faulty coil with ion circuit are further causes.

causes.label: Engine software or calibration
Spark plugs sooted, oily or wrong type or gap
Ignition coil or cassette with ion circuit faulty
Wiring or connector of the ion current return line

symptoms: Limp mode or reduced power possible

P0350.title: Ignition Coil Primary/Secondary Circuit/Open
P0350.description: P0350 is the general ignition coil circuit code without assignment to a coil: the engine module detects a fault in the primary or secondary circuit of a coil but does not report which one. This typically concerns older systems with a shared output stage or ignition module, or a shared feedback line for all coils. The monitoring works as for P0351 ff – primary-current feedback for each ignition command, or the voltage at the driver. GM and Ford report coil faults individually (P0351 ff, P2300 ff) and do not use P0350; the description follows CARB's output monitoring requirement, which allows one collective code.

causes.label: Ignition coil, coil pack or ignition module faulty
Shared supply (fuse, relay, ignition feed) or ground open
Harness, connector or feedback line to the coils faulty
Ignition lead or plug connector damaged (secondary side)
Engine module or driver

symptoms: Starting problems or stalling if a shared output stage fails

P0351.title: Ignition Coil A Primary Control Circuit/Open
P0351.description: Modern engines have one coil-on-plug ignition coil per cylinder, with the output stage either in the engine module or in the coil itself. P0351 monitors the primary control circuit of coil A – the line from the engine module to the coil or its built-in output stage – for an open circuit or high resistance. GM's module measures the voltage with its low-side driver off and flags an open circuit above 30 kΩ in 50 of 63 samples (2018 engines in the first trip, older ones after two); Ford checks continuously within 1 s, expecting a primary-current feedback for every ignition command, and shuts off injection to that cylinder for 30 s at a time. Short circuits and the secondary side have their own codes (P2300 ff). Coil A usually serves cylinder 1, but the assignment is up to the manufacturer.

causes.label: Ignition coil A faulty (output stage in the coil or primary winding open)
Connector at the coil corroded, loose or with a spread pin
Control, supply or ground wire open or chafed
Fuse or relay of the coil supply (then usually several codes)
Driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Misfire and rough running on cylinder 1, often also P0301
Loss of power, jerking under load
Cylinder shut off (injection off), risk to the catalyst if driven on

P0356.title: Ignition Coil F Primary Control Circuit/Open
P0356.description: P0356 monitors the primary control circuit of ignition coil F – the line from the engine module to the coil or to its built-in output stage – for an open circuit or high resistance. P0365.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Bank 1

P0370.title: Timing Reference High Resolution Signal A
P0370.description: Some diesel systems give the injection control a finely divided angle signal in addition to the normal reference signal, to time and meter injection precisely – the high resolution signal. GM's 6.5-litre diesel (1997) had an optical sensor in the injection pump that delivers a high resolution track and one cam reference pulse per cylinder; P0370 is set if more than 8 consecutive cam pulses pass without progress on the high resolution counter, in the first trip. The engine then runs on backup fuelling with reduced power, and injection timing control is suspended. On the 2004 Duramax LB7 the injector driver module evaluates the 57X crank signal and reports 'no crank signal' over CAN; from 60 rpm, 100 of 120 samples sets P0370, also in the first trip. Petrol engines practically do not use the code.

P0371.title: Timing Reference High Resolution Signal A Too Many Pulses

P0374.title: Timing Reference High Resolution Signal A No Pulses

Sensor disc or tone wheel damaged

P037A.title: Glow Plug/Heater Indicator Control Circuit Low
P037A.description: Diesel engines show the driver a wait-to-start lamp while the glow plugs preheat; the engine module switches it with a high-side driver. P037A means the lamp control circuit is too low – in practice a short to ground on the line to the instrument cluster. GM's diesels detect it in the driver itself: about 0.5 Ω to ground with the lamp commanded, only with a lamp configured, ignition on, more than 11 V and not while cranking. The 2015 engines need 3 s of fault, the 2016/2018 engines 10 of 15 samples; the check engine light follows after two trips. The glow plugs keep working; only the indication is missing, so the driver may start too early. CARB requires monitoring of the wait-to-start lamp circuit. Ford reports lamp faults under P0381 and does not use P037A.

causes.label: Lamp control wire chafed through to ground between engine module and cluster
Lamp or LED driver in the instrument cluster shorted internally
Moisture or corrosion in the module or cluster connector
Driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Glow plug light does not come on or stays dim
Check engine light on (GM after two trips)
Driver starts too early, possibly poor cold start

P037B.title: Glow Plug/Heater Indicator Control Circuit High
P037B.description: P037B is the counterpart of P037A: the control circuit of the wait-to-start lamp is too high, i.e. the line carries voltage although the engine module's driver is off, or the driver sees a short to battery voltage. GM's 2015 diesels check in the off state and set the fault after 1 s with more than 11 V; the 2016/2018 engines evaluate a short of about 0.5 Ω to a voltage source in the driver, 10 of 20 samples at 100 ms. In both cases the check engine light comes on after two trips. The lamp then stays on permanently or cannot be switched off, so the driver no longer gets a usable preheat signal; the driver may protect itself when commanded. There is no limp mode. Ford and Saab do not use P037B; CARB requires monitoring of the lamp circuit and of output components for shorts.

causes.label: Lamp control wire chafed against battery or ignition positive
Fault in the instrument cluster feeding voltage back
Water damage in a connector bridging to a neighbouring pin
Driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Glow plug light stays on or flickers

P037C.title: Cold Start Camshaft Profile System Performance
P037C.description: To heat the catalyst quickly after a cold start, some engines select a particular camshaft profile; CARB counts altered valve timing among these cold-start measures and requires components of the cold-start strategy to have their own diagnostics. P037C checks whether the requested profile is actually engaged during this phase. It is documented by code only at GM, on the 2.7-litre turbo four-cylinder (L3B) with a three-step sliding camshaft: while catalyst heating is active, the measured lift state is compared with the cold-start target, and if it is wrong in 100 of 120 cylinder events the code is set in the first trip. Two GM bulletins (19-NA-145 for 2019 Silverado/Sierra 1500 with stalling on remote start below −6 °C, 20-NA-174 for the 2020 Cadillac CT4) trace P037C to a software fault and reprogram the engine module.

causes.label: Engine module software (GM L3B, reprogramming)
Profile actuator (sliding cam pin) sticking or not switching
Actuator circuit (connector, wiring)
Wrong oil viscosity or low oil level, mechanism stiff when cold

symptoms: Rough running or stalling when cold (for example on remote start)

P037D.title: Glow Plug Sense Circuit
P037D.description: To check the glow plugs, the engine module reads back the voltage or current of the glow plug supply through a sense circuit – CARB requires glow plug circuits to be monitored for correct current and voltage drop, and from model year 2010 the failure of a single plug to be detected. In the J2012 scheme P037D is the general code for this sense circuit, P037E and P037F its low and high counterparts. None of the manufacturer documents available to us uses P037D: GM's 2016/2018 diesels use only P037E/P037F, Ford 2023 its own glow plug codes (P0671 ff, P064C) and Saab reports the feedback of its glow plug control module as P0380/P0382. The description therefore follows CARB and the GM sister codes. Typically glow plug monitoring is inactive; glowing itself can work normally.

causes.label: Sense wire open or high resistance, connector corroded
Glow relay or glow plug control module giving an implausible feedback
Fuse or fusible link of the glow plug supply blown
Engine module internal

symptoms: Check engine light or glow plug light on
Possibly poor cold start if the cause also affects the glow plug supply

P037E.title: Glow Plug Sense Circuit Low
P037E.description: P037E means the voltage read back from the glow plug supply is too low. GM's 2016/2018 diesels, whose glow plug output stages sit in the engine module, compare the feedback with the battery voltage while glowing: if it is lower by more than a calibrated, current-dependent threshold – excessive voltage drop or a short to ground of the sense line – a sample counts as faulty, and 60 of 120 samples in a 50 ms grid set the code, roughly 3 of 6 s. The check only runs with the engine running (afterglow), not while cranking, and is suspended if a single plug or the supply already has an electrical fault. GM classes the cause as internal to the module (measuring circuit) and turns on the check engine light after two trips. There is no limp mode; glow plug monitoring is restricted.

causes.label: High contact resistance in the glow plug supply (connector, ground, fusible link)
Measuring circuit or output stage in the engine module
Sense or supply wire shorted to ground
Weak battery or vehicle voltage at the edge of the enable range

symptoms: Possibly hard starting or knocking when cold

P037F.title: Glow Plug Sense Circuit High
P037F.description: P037F means the voltage read back from the glow plug supply is too high. GM's 2016/2018 diesels set it when the feedback lies above a threshold derived from the run/crank relay voltage, with a feedback above 5.0 V – for example voltage is reported although the plugs are not energised, or the sense line is shorted to positive. The code needs 40 of 80 samples at 50 ms, about 2 of 4 s, only with the engine running, and turns on the check engine light after two trips; GM classes the cause as internal to the module. If there is a real short to positive or a stuck relay or output stage, the plugs can stay energised permanently, overheating them and draining the battery – then also check the single plug codes P0671 ff and P066x. CARB requires glow plug circuits to be monitored for correct current and voltage drop.

causes.label: Sense wire chafed against positive or bridged in the connector
Glow relay sticking or output stage shorted (supply stays on)
Measuring circuit in the engine module

symptoms: Glow plugs possibly energised permanently (flat battery, plug damage)

P0380.title: Glow Plug/Heater Circuit A
P0380.description: P0380 concerns glow plug circuit A – depending on the manufacturer the first group of plugs, glow relay 1 or feedback line A of the glow plug control module. Saab's 3.0 TiD (9-5, 2002) has two feedback lines from the control module; if line A at the engine module stays above 4.0 V for more than 3 s while glowing, the module is reporting a plug or circuit fault, checked once per drive cycle with the warning lamp on. In Saab's 1.9 TiD (EDC16) the glow plug control module drives two pairs of plugs, monitors them itself and reports faults over a diagnostic line that should switch inversely to the activation line. The 2010/11 Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD sets P0380 for implausible feedback or a missing supply of the module, there without check engine light. Newer GM and Ford diesels report single plugs under P0671 ff instead.

causes.label: Glow plug(s) in circuit A burnt out
Glow plug control module or glow relay faulty
Wiring or connector fault (feedback line, plug connector, supply)
Missing battery or ignition supply of the control module (fuse)

symptoms: Hard starting when cold, long cranking
White or blue smoke and rough running after a cold start
Glow plug light or check engine light on or flashing

P0381.title: Glow Plug/Heater Indicator Control Circuit/Open
P0381.description: P0381 monitors the circuit of the wait-to-start lamp for an open circuit or, more generally, for faults that keep the lamp dark when commanded – CARB names a burnt-out bulb as the example, with exemptions for LCD clusters and for engines that only release the starter after preheating. GM's 2015–2018 diesels detect an open circuit in the driver by a high load impedance (about 200 kΩ in 2015), in 0.2 s or 10 of 15 samples, with the check engine light after two trips; on the 2014 Duramax LML P0381 still covered all lamp circuit faults including a short to ground. Ford's 2023 diesels check via the instrument cluster: if it reports the lamp off although on is commanded, P0381 is set within about 1 s at key-on. There is no limp mode; the risk is starting too early in the cold.

Lamp or LED in the instrument cluster burnt out
Instrument cluster faulty or communication problem (Ford)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Glow plug light does not come on at key-on
Check engine light on (GM after two trips)
Driver starts too early in the cold

P0382.title: Glow Plug/Heater Circuit B
P0382.description: P0382 is the counterpart of P0380 for glow plug circuit B – depending on the manufacturer the second group of plugs, glow relay 2 or feedback line B of the glow plug control module. A code-specific manufacturer description exists from Saab: the 3.0 TiD V6 diesel in the 9-5 (2002) reads two feedback lines from its glow plug control module, and if line B stays above 4.0 V for more than 3 s while glowing, the module is reporting a fault in the second group of plugs; the check runs once per drive cycle, the warning lamp comes on and there is no further system reaction. Newer GM and Ford diesels report single plugs under P0671 ff and do not use P0382. CARB requires glow plug circuits to be monitored for correct current and voltage drop. The typical consequence is a poor cold start with smoke.

P0383.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Control Circuit Low
P0383.description: Many diesels have a separate glow plug control module that the engine module commands over a control line. P0383 means this line is too low. In GM's logic for the 2010/11 Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD the engine module drives the module with a PWM signal and holds about 10 V on the line at rest (9.5–10.5 V at the signal terminal); if it reads too little voltage for more than 0.5 s – short to ground, or an open circuit or high resistance – it sets P0383, with ignition on, 9–16 V, once per ignition cycle. In that European version the code does not turn on the check engine light. Without a valid command the module does not glow, so the engine starts poorly when cold. Ford uses P0384 differently and not P0383; GM's 2016/2018 diesels have their output stages in the engine module and no such line. For US vehicles there is no code-specific source.

Corroded connector at the glow plug module in the engine bay
Glow plug control module faulty (input pulls the line down)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Warning lamp depending on the manufacturer

P0384.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Control Circuit High
P0384.description: P0384 is the counterpart of P0383: the control line from the engine module to the glow plug control module is too high, i.e. shorted to positive. In GM's logic for the 2010/11 Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD the signal terminal should show 9.5–10.5 V; a higher voltage for more than 0.5 s, with ignition on and 9–16 V, sets the code, there without check engine light. Ford's 2023 diesels (6.7 and 3.0 litre) use P0384 differently from the J2012 name, for the supply voltage of the glow plug module: below 6.5 V, above 16.5 V or open, detected in about 1 s – today J2012 has P052F for that. So with Ford, check battery, alternator and the module's supply first. The consequence is missing or irregular preheating or a protective shutdown of the module, with a poor cold start.

causes.label: Control line chafed against positive or bridged in the connector
Glow plug control module faulty internally (feeding back)
Ford: supply of the module outside 6.5–16.5 V or open (battery, alternator, fuse)
Engine module

symptoms: No or irregular preheating, hard starting when cold
Warning lamp depending on the manufacturer

P0385.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit
P0385.description: Some engines have a second crankshaft sensor or a second track on the tone wheel, which the engine module checks against sensor A or the camshaft. P0385 means its signal is missing or does not match. GM's 2004 Northstar 4.6 V8 counts the crank pulses per cam pulse (target 48 ± 1, fault in 8 of 10 tests) and also flags 2 s while cranking or 0.4 s running without a match, after two trips; an active P0385 suspends the cam sensor check. GM's 3.8-litre V6 (2006) sets it when its low resolution track stays silent while the medium resolution track delivers 36 pulses, 40 of 50 samples. The Honda 3.5-litre in the 2004 Saturn Vue Redline sets it when the second crank signal is missing while the first runs, judged after 17 revolutions, in the first trip. The engine usually keeps running on sensor A.

causes.label: Crankshaft position sensor B faulty
Connector or wiring open or corroded
Tone wheel or second track damaged
Engine module

P0386.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0386.description: P0386 means the signal of the second crankshaft sensor or second tone wheel track is present but implausible. GM's 2004 Northstar 4.6 V8 sets it after 5 resynchronisations within 10 s, after two trips. GM's 3.8-litre V6 (2006) expects exactly 0 or 6 low resolution pulses per 36 medium resolution pulses and one cam pulse; any other count in 40 of 50 samples sets the code, also after two trips. The Honda 3.5-litre in the 2004 Saturn Vue Redline counts implausible signals of its second crank sensor (target 44 crank pulses per 3 cam pulses, checked every half revolution, the counter dropping by one every 10 s) and sets the code at 30, about 2.2 s at idle, in the first trip. Typical causes are interference pulses, a dirty sensor or a wrong air gap; the result is jerking, misfire or longer cranking.

causes.label: Interference pulses (wiring near the ignition, shielding)
Sensor dirty or air gap wrong
Tone wheel damaged
Sensor faulty

P0387.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P0387.description: By its J2012 name P0387 means the signal of the second crankshaft sensor stays at a low level – typically a short to ground of the signal wire, a missing or shorted sensor supply, or with an inductive sensor an amplitude that is too small. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0387: the engines with a sensor B that we found (GM Northstar 4.6 and 3.8-litre V6, the Honda 3.5-litre in the Saturn Vue Redline) report its electrical faults under P0385 and implausible signals under P0386. The description therefore follows the J2012 name, the function of sensor B and CARB's monitoring requirement for crank angle sensors. As long as sensor A works, the engine usually keeps running; together with a sensor A fault it may not start.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor faulty
Sensor supply too low or shorted
Engine module

symptoms: Rough running, no start if sensor A also fails

P0388.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit High
P0388.description: Some engines have a second crankshaft sensor or a second track on the tone wheel – GM's 3.4/3.5/3.8-litre V6 use the low resolution track of a dual Hall sensor, the Honda 3.5-litre in the Saturn Vue Redline a second sensor – which the engine module checks against sensor A or the camshaft. By its J2012 name P0388 means the signal of sensor B stays above its upper limit – with a Hall sensor typically an open signal wire held high by the module's pull-up, or a short to positive. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0388: the engines with a sensor B report its electrical faults under P0385 and implausible signals under P0386. The description therefore follows the J2012 name, these component sources and CARB's monitoring requirement for crank angle sensors. The engine usually keeps running on sensor A; longer cranking is possible.

causes.label: Signal wire of sensor B open or connector corroded or loose
Signal wire shorted to positive or reference voltage
Sensor ground open
Sensor B faulty internally
Engine module input

symptoms: Often no noticeable symptoms while sensor A takes over

P0389.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P0389.description: Some engines have a second crankshaft sensor or a second track on the tone wheel – GM's 3.4/3.5/3.8-litre V6 use the low resolution track of a dual Hall sensor, the Honda 3.5-litre in the Saturn Vue Redline a second sensor – which the engine module checks against sensor A or the camshaft. By its J2012 name P0389 means the signal of sensor B drops out for moments or becomes erratic – missing or extra edges – without staying permanently low or high. Such faults are typically found by counting pulses against sensor A or the camshaft, as GM's 3.8-litre V6 and the Honda engine do; both, however, report the result under P0385/P0386, and no manufacturer document available to us uses P0389. The description therefore follows the J2012 name, these component sources and CARB. Typical causes are a loose contact, a broken wire and interference.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor B connector
Wire break or chafing that appears with engine movement
Electrical interference (add-on devices, routing near ignition or relays)
Tone wheel damaged or dirty, air gap too large
Sensor faulty, temperature-dependent

symptoms: Check engine light on, possibly only after several trips

P038A.title: Ignition I Control Signal Circuit/Open
P038A.description: Ignition I is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff). P038A means the control line is open – the module sees a voltage with its driver off that indicates high resistance. No manufacturer using these codes was found – neither GM nor Ford use the Ignition A to J codes; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff – so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.

causes.label: Control line or connector pin open (corrosion, pushed-back pin)
Ignition module or coil with integrated driver of this group faulty
Supply or ground of the ignition module faulty
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power, possibly cylinders shut off

P0390.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Bank 2
P0390.description: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0390 means no or too few exhaust cam pulses arrive from bank 2 while the crankshaft turns. GM's 3.0 twin-turbo V6 (LGW) sets it after 5.5 s without a cam pulse, 4 s of cranking or fewer than 4 pulses in 3 s, after two trips; for GM it collects all circuit faults. Ford checks the crank-to-cam ratio from 200 rpm within 5 s, and the 2004 Northstar counts missing signal changes up to 16. Driver in the engine module
